question:
A company offers three schemes of successive discounts. 

First: 25%, 10%

Second: 20 %, 15%

Third: 30%, 5%

Which scheme is best for the company?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the sum of two successive discounts is constant (35% in all cases), the equivalent discount is minimum when their product is maximum.

Product of discounts: First = 25 × 10 = 250, Second = 20 × 15 = 300, Third = 30 × 5 = 150.

The Second scheme has the maximum product (300), hence it gives the minimum equivalent discount.

A minimum discount to the customer means maximum profit and highest selling price for the company.

**∴ The correct answer is Second scheme.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First scheme: 25% and 10%

Second scheme: 20% and 15%

Third scheme: 30% and 5%

**Formula Used:**

Equivalent Discount = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)
